Hi Neha,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are Globex's DPA redlines — our security team flagged a few items we need clarity on before we can proceed to signature:

- Key management: does Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for hosted accounts, or only for Dedicated/Private? Our standard is BYOK with CloudHSM backing for any data exported outside the EU.
- Key rotation & escrow: we need a documented rotation policy and assurance around key escrow/compromise handling.
- Export controls/data transfers: we require confirmation of the mechanism you intend to rely on for EU->US transfers (SCCs, DPF, or other).
- Subprocessors: an ask to limit subcontractor changes without 30 days' notice and to provide SOC2 evidence for infra providers.
- TOMs exhibit: we have a few edits (encryption specifics, privileged access controls) — see redlines.

Can you confirm which items you can accept as-is, which you want to counter, and whether you'd be able to sign via DocuSign? We need to finalize legal/infosec approvals next week.

Thanks,
Sigrid Holm
Senior Counsel, Globex Corp

Hi Sigrid — thanks for the clear redlines and the list. We're aligned on getting this wrapped quickly. High-level responses here; I'll follow up with a consolidated DPA that incorporates agreed TOMs edits for signature.

1) Customer-managed keys (BYOK):
   - For Dedicated and Private deployments we already support BYOK with HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Key Vault HSM).
   - For Hosted (standard multi-tenant) we do NOT offer full BYOK today, but we provide envelope encryption and per-tenant key separation; we can offer a managed KMS path with strict access controls and quarterly key rotation. If BYOK is required for Hosted, we'd need a separate scoped contract and an engineering schedule (typically a 6–10 week integration).

2) Key rotation & compromise:
   - Our standard rotation cadence for platform-managed keys is 90 days; customer-managed keys follow the customer's rotation. In case of compromise we provide immediate key reissue and forensic logs; Lauren (legal) will detail SLA/notification language.

3) Data transfer mechanism:
   - Our standard approach is SCCs for EU transfers with DPF as fallback where customers opt-in. We can include explicit language in the DPA.

4) Subprocessors:
   - We can commit to 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and to providing SOC 2 Type II reports for major infra vendors.

5) TOMs exhibit edits:
   - Attached is Redwood_TOMs_Exhibit_v2.docx with proposed wording for encryption (AES-256), privileged access controls (RBAC + short-lived creds), and key management options.

If this aligns, I'll generate a consolidated DPA and send a DocuSign link. If Globex prefers AdobeSign, we can do that as well — both are supported.

Next steps: please confirm you can accept SCCs + DPF fallback and whether Hosted BYOK is a hard requirement.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Neha / Markus — quick legal guidance after reviewing Globex redlines and the TOMs draft. Proposed positions: 

- BYOK: Accept for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, counter-offer: managed envelope encryption + contractual commitments around separation and access; allow BYOK for Hosted only under an addendum with engineering lead time and a limited fee.
- HSM requirement for cross-border exports: we can accept HSM-backed KMS for customer keys used to protect exported data (meets Globex ask).
- Key rotation: document 90-day rotation for platform keys; allow customer to set rotation for BYOK.
- Key escrow/compromise: we should preserve incident notification windows (48 hours initial notice) and provide for forensic logs export under NDA.
- Subprocessors: agree to 30 days' notice and SOC2 Type II for infra providers; carve out limited emergency onboarding with notification.

I'll insert these positions into the consolidated DPA and TOMs exhibit. For signatures, DocuSign is our default; AdobeSign acceptable as alternative.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Hi Sigrid — thanks for working through the redlines. Attached is a consolidated DPA that reflects the following agreed points: 

- Encryption: AES-256 at rest + TLS1.2+ in transit; envelope encryption for multi-tenant hosted customers.
- Key management:
   • Dedicated/Private: full BYOK supported with HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Key Vault HSM).
   • Hosted: managed KMS with per-tenant envelope encryption by default; Hosted BYOK available under a scoped addendum (engineering lead time 6–10 weeks + setup fee).
   • Rotation: platform-managed keys rotate every 90 days; customers control rotation for BYOK.
   • Compromise response: 48-hour initial notification, immediate key reissue, forensic logs export under NDA.
- Access controls: RBAC, short-lived credentials for platform admins, periodic privileged-access reviews (90-day cadence).
- Subprocessors: 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors; SOC2 Type II reports available on request; emergency onboarding carve-out with notification.
- Data transfers: SCCs as primary mechanism; DPF fallback where used by the customer.

I've uploaded the consolidated DPA for signature via DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-ef12-3456
Please confirm the signers and whether you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign. If this looks good we can have the DPA executed today and start the procurement/technical onboarding sprint.

Attachments included: Consolidated_DPA_for_Signature_20270315.pdf (the TOMs exhibit is embedded).
